title: CyberAlchemy Lab: permission, meaning and agent work
case: Fictional customer-export capability delivery. Fully specified reader-facing definition content is shown before illustrative owner acceptance; separate implementation and review assignments and permissions follow. No canonical Lab records or actual runs are asserted.
model_boundaries: An accepted exact definition governs meaning within owner scope.
An assignment identifies the work. Current permission governs agent actions.
Provenance preserves inputs and production history. Evidence supports the stated, bounded claim.
Each record keeps its own lifecycle. Candidate repair, review and authorized activation remain distinct.
Machine agents are temporary. Short-term memory belongs to the session. Long-term memory is Project State, recovered through context and ontology views.
design_source: The documentation site’s KEP logo, transparent orb and palette.
edition: Definition-first product capability, implementation and review carousel
diagram_roles: Permission alone does not settle what complete means. Three governance lenses introduce rules, origin and lifecycle.
A generic customer needs an active-record export. Define the outcome, then write code and review output.
Customer 1 active records qualify; Customer 1 inactive records and Customer 2 active records do not. The rule covers every matching ID across the full source.
The authorized requirements owner accepts the definition. One accepted meaning guides both agents.
The accepted meaning is separate from each agent’s scoped actions. Neither may redefine it or put code into use.
The exact saved source, code and saved export form a trace. Review uses the accepted definition to compare each required ID: 10,000 required, 9,800 present and 200 missing.
Temporary work/review sessions record under project rules. Later sessions receive selected records and their connections from shared Project State with separately granted permissions.
The definition is already accepted. Candidate code has a review gap; revision/review, exact owner acceptance and separately permitted use form a conditional future route.
Authority, provenance and lifecycle connect around shared knowledge. A website-release invitation closes the sequence.

external_context.title: NIST AI RMF Core
external_context.editorial_use: Governance frameworks already cover accountability, policies and lifecycle. The contrast concerns the familiar permissions/compliance framing and the Lab’s explicit record architecture, without claiming exclusive ownership of broader governance.

positioning: Provocative conditional framing targets governance that stops at authorization, permissions and compliance. It does not claim that common governance frameworks universally exclude meanings, evidence or lifecycle, and makes no legal-compliance claim.
clarity_revision: Overview → authored definition content → exact owner acceptance → implementation/review jobs and permissions → evidence → lifecycle → durable project state.
caption_revision: Short provocative caption foregrounding permissions/privacy limits, exact scoped meaning authority and the reviewer’s missing-ID result.
definition_completeness_ceiling: The shown sheet fully states the illustrative outcome and coverage criterion. It is not presented as a schema-complete, registry-synchronized canonical Lab Definition; structural completeness and admission remain separate in the source model.
language_revision: Familiar language across every slide, diagram description and caption. Database entries and a saved database copy replace source records and source data. Formal model records and exact ID-selection semantics remain unchanged.
reader_facing_term: Complete customer export, scoped explicitly to required record identifier coverage. The internal exact example retains the term ID-complete customer export.
required_ids_revision: Required identifiers are selected from every record in the fixed source snapshot belonging to the chosen account and satisfying every declared filter. The fictional source includes matching records and excluded inactive/other-account records. The review compares the derived required set with the export, rather than inferring requirements from the export.

explained: Record IDs uniquely identify source records.
The source data is saved at one moment so later updates do not change the comparison.
Required records belong to the chosen account and satisfy every filter, illustrated by Customer 1 and active status.
The semantic owner is the person authorized to set the service’s requirements.
Completeness here checks required ID coverage, excluding value accuracy, duplicates and extra IDs.
The reviewer compares identifier membership rather than assuming counts establish coverage.
Deployment is described as putting accepted code into use and requires separate permission.
Each agent exists for a temporary work session. Short-term memory belongs to the session.
Recorded work becomes part of shared Project State through project recording rules. Later agents receive selected records and their connections, with separate permissions.

sequence: Exact source, code, output and definition tied to review
Candidate code and conditional acceptance/use transitions
Temporary sessions and governed recording into shared project state

semantic_boundaries: Required IDs derive from the full saved source, chosen customer account and all filters, independently of the export.
The review checks membership of each required ID. Counts and coverage bar summarize that check.
The meaning owner accepts the exact scoped definition. This neither proves implementation conformance nor grants action permissions.
Definition and implementation keep separate lifecycles. Later code acceptance and permission to use are conditional and separate.
Private session memory ends with the ephemeral machine agent. Project State supplies later context and ontology projections; recording and new permissions remain governed.
